text: Naughty Dog, LLC (formerly JAM Software, Inc.), is an American first-party video game developer based in Santa Monica, California. Founded by Andy Gavin and Jason Rubin in 1984, the studio was acquired by Sony Computer Entertainment in 2001. Gavin and Rubin created a series of successful games, including Rings of Power and Way of the Warrior in the early 1990s; the latter prompted Universal Interactive Studios to sign them for a three-title contract and fund company expansion. After Mark Cerny convinced Naughty Dog to develop a character-based 3D platform game for new consoles, the studio created Crash Bandicoot for the PlayStation in 1996, releasing three titles over the following years. Following Crash Team Racing, they developed Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy for the PlayStation 2. In 2004, Rubin, who had become president, left to work on The Iron Saint. Naughty Dog also hosts the ICE Team, a central technology group within PlayStation Studios, originally named Initiative for a Common Engine, which develops core graphics technologies and supports both first-party and third-party developers. The studio's first PlayStation 3 game, Uncharted: Drake's Fortune, was released in 2007, followed by several sequels and spin-offs, and later, the new intellectual property The Last of Us, developed by a secondary team and released in 2013 to critical acclaim, spawning a franchise. The Last of Us Part II was released for the PlayStation 4 in 2020 to similar acclaim. The studio is currently developing Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet for the PlayStation 5. Gavin and Rubin met as pre-teens in 1982 at a Hebrew school in Virginia, where they developed an interest in computers and video games. They founded JAM Software in 1984 with friend Mike Goyet, using the acronym "Jason, Andy and Mike," which was later changed to "Jason and Andy's Magic" after Goyet withdrew. They created Ski Crazed, originally titled Ski Stud, after accidentally losing their skiing game copy; the game sold over 1,000 copies after being published by Baudville for $250. They also released Dream Zone in 1988 for the Apple IIGS, ported to Atari ST, Amiga, and PCs. In 1989, they renamed JAM Software to Naughty Dog on September 9. They released Keef the Thief in 1989 for Apple IIGS, Amiga, and PCs, and developed Rings of Power for the Sega Genesis in 1991 with programmer Vijay Pande. In 1994, they released Way of the Warrior for the 3DO, which led to a three-game contract with Universal Interactive Studios. They devised a 3D action-platform game, jokingly named "Sonic's Ass Game," which took 14 months to develop, involved the creation of Game Oriented Object Lisp, and featured characters designed by Charles Zembillas and Joe Pearson, resulting in Crash Bandicoot. The game was shown to Sony, who published it, and became one of the PlayStation's highest-selling titles, selling over 6.8 million copies. Naughty Dog later released two more Crash Bandicoot titles and the spin-off Crash Team Racing. Sony acquired the studio in 2001, partly due to rising development costs—first games had budgets of around $50,000, while Crash Bandicoot reached $1.5 million—providing the stability needed for continued development. The Jak and Daxter series, developed initially by Naughty Dog, achieved similar success to Crash Bandicoot. During development of Jak 3 and Jak X: Combat Racing, Rubin and Gavin transitioned Evan Wells and Stephen White to co-presidents, with White later replaced by Christophe Balestra. In 2007, Naughty Dog launched the Uncharted series, marking a shift toward realistic worlds and characters, which sold over 41 million copies worldwide by December 2017. In 2011, Naughty Dog unveiled The Last of Us, a post-apocalyptic third-person action-adventure game following Ellie and Joel in a world infected by a Cordyceps-like disease. The game received universal acclaim upon release. In 2012 and 2013, Naughty Dog partnered with Mass Media Inc. to release the Jak and Daxter Collection, high-definition ports of the original PlayStation 2 trilogy for PlayStation 3 and Vita. In May 2013, Naughty Dog confirmed it would continue using its existing in-house engine for PlayStation 4. On November 23, 2013, Corrinne Yu joined Naughty Dog from 343 Industries. On December 7, 2013, Naughty Dog won Studio of the Year at Spike's VGX for The Last of Us. In March 2014, Uncharted lead writer Amy Hennig left, followed by Uncharted 3 director Justin Richmond and The Last of Us lead artist Nate Wells. A remastered version of The Last of Us was later released on PlayStation 4. In March 2017, Balestra announced his retirement as co-president on April 3, 2017, after 15 years, with Evan Wells remaining president. In September 2017, Bruce Straley departed, citing a sabbatical. Neil Druckmann was promoted to vice president in March 2018. In October 2017, David Ballard claimed he suffered a mental breakdown due to sexual harassment by a senior team member in late 2015, reported to HR, and was terminated the next day with a $20,000 silence offer, which he declined. Naughty Dog stated it had "not found any evidence" of harassment allegations. In December 2020, Neil Druckmann was promoted to co-president alongside Evan Wells; Alison Mori and Christian Gyrling were promoted to co-vice presidents. On October 4, 2021, Arne Meyer was promoted to co-vice president. In July 2022, Josh Scherr left after 21 years. In July 2023, Wells announced his retirement by year's end; Druckmann became head of creative, Mori became studio manager and head of operations, Meyer became head of culture and communications, and Gyrling became head of technology. The leadership team expanded with Erick Pangilinan and Jeremy Yates as co-heads of art, and Anthony Newman as head of production and design. In November 2023, Gyrling departed after 17 years, replaced by Travis McIntosh as head of technology. Naughty Dog is best known for its PlayStation console games, including Crash Bandicoot, Jak and Daxter, Uncharted, and The Last of Us. Before that, it developed Dream Zone, Keef the Thief, Rings of Power, and Way of the Warrior. The studio operates without a producer or middle-management, relying on minimal oversight. Naughty Dog won Studio of the Year at the 2013 VGX, the 2013 Golden Joystick Awards, and the 2020 Golden Joystick Awards.
